question: Is the landed floor of 2026-05-23 in fongniao_raw.raw_orders a property of the authoritative upstream source, or an artifact of the ingestion windows that have been run so far?
answer: ARTIFACT. The upstream holds 2 years of authoritative order history that has never been requested.

method.where: in-cluster Pod, GKE oday-dev, private-pool node, digest-pinned release image
method.writes: none - the probe has no write path and never touches PostgreSQL
method.predicate: Byte-for-byte the production window predicate from apps/data_platform/source.py::MongoSource._window_query for a non-snapshot kind: {"$or": [{"updatedAt": {"$gte": start, "$lt": end}}, {"createdAt": {"$gte": start, "$lt": end}}]}
method.redaction: Aggregates and two timestamps only. No order id, merchant, store, member, amount, or payload field is selected anywhere in the probe.

findings.finding: The upstream orders collection holds 2170979 documents with min createdAt 2024-06-26T13:33:27Z - about two years of authoritative history. The landed raw table holds 478265 rows, none older than 2026-05-23.

min(source_updated_at) is 2026-05-23T00:00:02.915Z, 2.9 seconds after the 2026-05-23T00:00:00Z lower bound of the very first orders-history window. A natural data boundary would not land 2.9s past a requested bound. min(observed_at) is 2026-07-24T18:37Z, so every raw row was landed by the 07-24 job or later. Nothing older than 2026-05-23 has ever been asked for.

The 2026-05-23 floor traces to infra/k8s/data-platform/render.py, which renders ODP_ORDERS_HISTORY_START as end - 62 days. The first job ran with end = 2026-07-24, and 2026-07-24 minus 62 days is exactly 2026-05-23. The floor is the default window, not the source.

Days immediately below the floor are dense and continuous - 6307 to 11011 orders per day across 2026-05-14..2026-05-22, and 179503 orders in 2026-05-01..2026-05-23. Monthly volume is 115k-252k back through at least 2025-11. Backwards extension lands real, dense history, not a sparse tail.

The upstream is MongoDB Atlas and its IP allowlist admits only the private-pool node pool's Cloud NAT egress. An identical probe pinned to default-pool failed with ServerSelectionTimeoutError against all three replica-set members. This is why the probe must share the one private-pool node with the backfill slices, and why it is sized to fit in the ~100Mi that remains while a slice is active.

consequence.supersedes: The section 6 conclusion that criterion 3 is unreachable without a human-approved destructive delete against the source DB.
consequence.why: The 44-day cap was measured against landed data and was real, but it was never a ceiling on the AVAILABLE authoritative history. Defect D permanently costs the two days 2026-07-05 and 2026-07-06, which splits the attested span. The repair-free alternative is to stop trying to bridge that split and instead grow the span that already sits BELOW it.
consequence.arithmetic: A date D is training-eligible only if D is attested and rows exist for D-28..D-1, so N contiguous attested days yield N-28 eligible dates. The attested span below the Defect D split currently runs 2026-05-23..2026-07-04 (~44 days), giving ~15 eligible dates - short of 28. Extending the span back to 2026-05-07 makes it 59 days, giving 31 eligible dates, which clears the 28-day horizon with margin and needs no delete, no approval, and no change to the view.
consequence.plan: Two further governed orders-history slices below the floor, each <= 8 daily partitions so it fits inside the 4h activeDeadlineSeconds that Defect C documents: b1 = 2026-05-15..2026-05-23, b2 = 2026-05-07..2026-05-15. A third, b3 = 2026-04-29..2026-05-07, is queued for margin.
